items.t: Calverhall is a City of North Vancouver residential neighbourhood of detached-house streets between Grand Boulevard at the west side and Brooksbank Avenue at the east side, with Keith Road on the south side. Exact boundary streets are not verified — City sources use the Calverhall name at neighbourhood level without a published street-by-street boundary description. Confirmed anchors are Keith Road and Brooksbank Avenue, shown in the routing of TransLink route 232, and Calverhall Street and Cloverley Street inside the pocket.
Where the condo stock actually concentrates: nowhere in Calverhall. There is no verified apartment-condo or townhome stock inside the sub-area at all.

Transit anchors: TransLink route 232 (Grouse Mountain / Phibbs Exchange) runs via Brooksbank Avenue, Keith Road, Upper Keith Road and Lonsdale Avenue at the area's south and east sides; route 255 runs via Grand Boulevard East, Keith Road, Fern Street and Lillooet Road toward Capilano University at the west and south sides. The SeaBus at Lonsdale Quay, south-west of the area, crosses to Waterfront Station in 12 minutes, every 15 minutes during the day.

Anchors beside the area: Brooksbank Elementary, 980 13th Street East, and Sutherland Secondary, 1860 Sutherland Avenue, are beside the area to the south-east; the new Cloverley Elementary (585 seats) opened in September 2026 in the adjoining Cloverley neighbourhood; the new Harry Jerome Community Recreation Centre, 130 East 23rd Street, opened July 25, 2026, south-west of the area; North Vancouver City Library is at 120 West 14th Street.
One secondary source states Greater Vancouver REALTORS® published no Calverhall condo or townhome benchmark for September 2026, which is consistent with there being no condo stock to benchmark.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Calverhall

items.t: City plans and zoning (City of North Vancouver — not the District's): Calverhall is governed by the City of North Vancouver Official Community Plan Bylaw, 2014, No. 8400 (amended December 8, 2025 by Amendment Bylaw 2025, No. 9114 for provincial housing requirements) and Zoning Bylaw, 1995, No. 6700.

The GO Zone — the attached form that is actually coming to Calverhall: the City adopted the Ground Oriented (GO) Zone on December 8, 2025, under Zoning Bylaw No. 6700 (Amendment Bylaw 2025, No. 9137): a lot of 280 m² or less allows up to 3 units, a larger lot allows up to 4 units in the Low Rise Neighbourhood 1 designation and up to 6 units in Low Rise Neighbourhood 2 or Residential Level 4 designations. City-wide, the change raised permitted units to 4 on nearly 4,300 residential properties and up to 6 per lot on approximately 600 properties. Future Calverhall "attached" purchases will most likely be strata or freehold units in these small multiplexes — none completed and named in the sub-area was verified yet.

Suites and coach houses: the City legalized secondary suites in all single-family dwellings in 1993; one suite is permitted per single-family property, the owner must reside at the property, and a suite may be combined with an accessory coach house where the front lot line is at least 10 m, with a Development Permit and a Building Permit. A coach-house approval here is a CITY approval — listing text that says "subject to District review" for a Calverhall address is misstating the approving municipality.

Streamside permits: the City's Streamside Protection Development Permit Area covers land within 15 metres of the top of bank of a watercourse or within 10 metres of the top of a ravine bank, and the City's stormwater plan names a creek channel from the Calverhall – Cloverly neighbourhoods — check creek-side lots before pricing a multiplex or coach-house build.

City tax timing: City of North Vancouver 2026 property taxes were due July 2, 2026; the 2026 total residential rate is 3.34028 per $1,000 of assessed value, plus a separate residential storm drainage rate of 0.10697 per $1,000.

Secondary sources label Calverhall "(District)," and a current listing for a Cloverley Street house describes coach-house potential as "subject to all District review/approval/permits" — for a City of North Vancouver address, the approving body is the City, under City Bylaw No. 6700.

The density arrived by bylaw, not by building. On December 8, 2025 the City adopted the GO Zone (Bylaw No. 9137), lifting permitted units to 4 on nearly 4,300 City properties and up to 6 on about 600 — Calverhall's future attached stock will be small strata multiplexes on today's house lots, and lot value now turns on the OCP designation, not on apartment zoning that does not exist here.

A new school opened next door in September 2026 — the first in North Vancouver in 35 years. Cloverley Elementary is a 585-seat school with 92 licensed child care spaces, in the adjoining Cloverley neighbourhood; its catchment review potentially redraws four existing elementary catchments around Calverhall. Note the spelling split in official sources: "Cloverley" (SD44 / Province) vs "Cloverly" (City stormwater plan) — search both.

The City's newest recreation centre opened the same summer. The Harry Jerome Community Recreation Centre, 130 East 23rd Street, opened July 25, 2026, south-west of the area — the amenity anchor for a neighbourhood that has no recreation facility inside its own streets.
Grand Boulevard is a heritage character area at the pocket's west edge.

The City's Integrated Stormwater Management Plan names a creek channel from the Calverhall – Cloverly neighbourhoods — the same document that proves the City geography — and the streamside permit area follows that channel. It is the lot-level check most Calverhall listings never mention.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Calverhall

items.t: Calverhall is a City of North Vancouver neighbourhood-level area between Grand Boulevard and Brooksbank Avenue, above Keith Road. Exact boundary streets are not verified — City sources use the Calverhall name at neighbourhood level without a published street-by-street boundary description; the confirmed anchors are Keith Road and Brooksbank Avenue on the south and east sides, shown in the routing of TransLink route 232, and the new Cloverley Elementary school site in the Cloverley neighbourhood beside it.

Nearby areas: Cloverley (east, with the new elementary school), Brooksbank / Sutherland (south-east), Grand Boulevard / Boulevard (west, across Grand Boulevard — Boulevard straddles the City/District line at Highway 1, but Calverhall itself is wholly City ground), Lower Lonsdale (south-west, down Keith Road), and the District's Lynn Valley side (north, across Highway 1).

Parks, recreation and services: no park, recreation centre or library branch inside this sub-area was confirmed on a City, school district or regional source — not verified. The City's Green Necklace system of boulevards and parks, including Grand Boulevard Park to the west, serves the wider central City. The new Harry Jerome Community Recreation Centre, 130 East 23rd Street, opened Saturday, July 25, 2026, south-west of the area. North Vancouver City Library, 120 West 14th Street, in Central Lonsdale serves Calverhall. Health care: Lions Gate Hospital, 231 East 15th Street; North Vancouver Urgent and Primary Care Centre, 2nd floor, 221 West Esplanade. Shopping: no shopping centre or grocery store for this sub-area was named on a City source — not verified; the City names Park & Tilford Shopping Centre east of the Grand Boulevard corridor, and the Lonsdale Avenue shops in Central Lonsdale are the City's main-street retail to the south-west.

Roads and transit: Keith Road and Brooksbank Avenue are the through roads on the south and east sides; Grand Boulevard runs north–south at the west side toward Highway 1. TransLink route 232 (Grouse Mountain / Phibbs Exchange) runs via Brooksbank Avenue, Keith Road, Upper Keith Road and Lonsdale Avenue at the area's south and east sides; route 255 runs via Grand Boulevard East, Keith Road, Fern Street and Lillooet Road toward Capilano University at the west and south sides. The SeaBus at Lonsdale Quay crosses to Waterfront Station in 12 minutes, every 15 minutes during the day.
City context only: the City's 2021 Census population was 58,120 and the City covers 11.83 km².

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Calverhall

items.t: Zoning — City Zoning Bylaw No. 6700, Ground Oriented (GO) Zone: the unit ladder and subdivision minimum widths in; the GO Zone was adopted December 8, 2025 (Amendment Bylaw 2025, No. 9137 in the City's housing record). District Zoning Bylaw 3210 does not apply on this City ground and is never imported here.

OCP — City Official Community Plan Bylaw, 2014, No. 8400: the City plan governing Calverhall, amended December 8, 2025 (Amendment Bylaw 2025, No. 9114) for provincial housing requirements; the lot's OCP designation (Low Rise Neighbourhood 1 vs 2 / Residential Level 4) decides the GO Zone unit count. A Calverhall-specific plan is not verified (none confirmed).

: Subdivision itself runs off the GO Zone minimum lot widths (7.5 m / 10.0 m corner in Low Rise Neighbourhood 1; 15.0 m in other designations) and the older RS-2 / RS-3 minimum lot areas where those zones still state them. Confirm subdivision and servicing requirements with the City for the specific parcel.

Streamside Development Permit (the live Calverhall check): land within 15 metres of a watercourse bank top or 10 metres of a ravine bank top needs a development permit before new development, and the City stormwater plan names a creek channel from the Calverhall – Cloverly neighbourhoods — run the check on creek-side lots before pricing a rebuild.
Heritage note: Grand Boulevard, at the area's west side, is a City heritage character area in the City heritage record; a heritage designation specific to Calverhall streets is not verified.

Strata block (for completeness — no Calverhall bare-land strata stock is verified): Form B diligence (provided within 7 days, max $35 + 25¢/page); depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws void since November 24, 2022 (short-term restrictions may still apply by bylaw); only 55+ age bylaws valid under SPA ss.123.1/123.2, with May 1, 2023 exemptions; a listing's "45+" line is not a valid BC age bylaw.

ALR rules (for completeness — no Calverhall ALR parcel is confirmed here): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; SPA s. 239; ALCA s. 21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Farm class is three-tiered ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by Oct 31) — a flat "$2,500+" line is an error.

City property taxes: City of North Vancouver 2026 property taxes were due July 2, 2026; the 2026 residential municipal-general rate is 1.89202 and the total residential rate is 3.34028 per $1,000 of assessed value, plus a separate residential storm drainage rate of 0.10697 per $1,000; the City illustrates an average residential property assessed at $1,387,684 paying $4,790 in total 2026 property taxes.

The density change is dated and City-wide in scale: the GO Zone adopted December 8, 2025 raised permitted units to 4 on nearly 4,300 City properties and up to 6 per lot on about 600 — a Calverhall lot priced off the old single-family zoning is priced off a repealed position; its OCP designation is the deciding fact.

The new school is a once-in-35-years event: Cloverley Elementary (585 seats, opened September 2026, with 92 licensed child care spaces) is the first elementary school to open in North Vancouver in 35 years — and its catchment review is exactly why no elementary assignment on these streets should be promised from an old listing.

Suites have been legal here since 1993: the City legalized secondary suites in all single-family dwellings in 1993 — three decades before the provincial SSMUH round — so a Calverhall suite history is a City record, not a recent conversion story.
